text:
maya: heads-up — seeing a sustained backlog on us-east GPU pool, admission control started rejecting ~10% of hosted API traffic and we started seeing 504/502 spikes

devon: timeline? metrics? any config changes before this?

maya: spike started ~2025-11-03T12:34:00Z, queue_depth jumped from ~90 -> 1300 over ~8m. we rolled the admission-control change ~45m earlier (lowered soft_admit_threshold to 0.85).

anita: ops-bot shows autoscaler executed but couldn't acquire new instances due to cloud quota on GPU family pn-rtx-a100.

ops-bot: autoscaler attempt at 2025-11-03T12:36:11Z failed: quota_exceeded (requested=32 gpus, quota=200, current_reserved=193)

ryan: reserved capacity for enterprise customers accounted for a lot of that reserved headroom yesterday. who changed the reservation?

maya: @ryan I opened a ticket last week to reserve capacity for AcmeCorp, change applied Tue 02:17 UTC by infra-team.

sre-lead: quick root-cause hypothesis: (1) an admission threshold change reduced admitted concurrency -> increased queue, (2) autoscaler attempted to scale but hit cloud quota -> scheduler started rerouting to fallback regions, (3) fallback regions saturated NAT/egress and began dropping connections -> client-side timeouts surfaced as 5xx/504s.

devon: paste queue/reject log snippet pls, need exact numbers for postmortem.

maya: logs snippet:
```
pool=us-east-gpu time=2025-11-03T12:34:05Z queue_depth=1340 admitted=1200 rejected=140 adm_threshold=0.85 autoscale_attempt=32gpus->fail quota=200 reserved=193
pool=us-east-gpu time=2025-11-03T12:36:05Z rpc_errors=72 network_errors=18 fallback_routed=1200
```

anita: routing policy had fallback=nearest-region and preserve_latency=true which sent a heavy burst to eu-west and us-west; those regions have smaller egress NAT throughput and started TCP-resetting under load.

ryan: we should have a circuit-breaker on fallback routing to slow reroute rate. we don't want a fanout loop where one saturated pool pushes load to others until everything struggles.

maya: mitigations executed: (1) increased soft_admit_threshold back to 0.95 at 2025-11-03T12:40:00Z, (2) disabled cross-region fallback at 12:42:10Z, (3) manually freed 10 reserved GPUs by moving AcmeCorp to their dedicated pool at 12:50:00Z.

devon: post-mitigation: queue drained by ~12:58 and 5xx/504 errors returned to baseline by ~13:05. tail latency remained elevated for ~30m.

sre-lead: impact summary: ~18m of elevated 5xxs for hosted API, ~0.6% of global requests affected, several enterprise customers observed retries and higher latency. no user data loss.

anita: action items:
- Infra: add fallback rate limit / routing circuit-breaker (owner: ryan, due: 2025-11-10)
- Product: require canary rollout for admission-threshold changes on low-traffic pools (owner: maya, due: 2025-11-07)
- Finance/Sales: review reserved capacity allocation for enterprise accounts; return 10 GPUs from AcmeCorp and add visibility on reservations (owner: ryan & sales, due: 2025-11-12)
- Infra: add autoscaler preflight to check cloud quota before provisioning requests (owner: devon, due: 2025-11-05)

maya: note for postmortem: traffic delta vs baseline was ~3.8x for short-seq workloads during spike window. top affected models: gpt-slim-v1, reranker-2025, embed-lite.

devon: I'll draft timeline + metrics and open PR for the postmortem doc. tagging folks for review :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout detected: infra/admission-control v1.12 -> v1.13 at 2025-11-03T11:49:02Z by infra-batch.

sre-lead: link the rollout in the postmortem and mark it as a contributing factor.

maya: will own incident writeup and coordinate RCA meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC. please add anything missed here.
